content: In medical terminology, the term dermatosis refers to any disease of the skin. The plural form of this term is dermatoses. It is important to differentiate dermatosis from dermatitis, as the latter specifically refers to inflammation of the skin. While the two terms are related, they are not synonymous. Dermatoses encompass all skin diseases, many of which are not contagious. Dermatitis, on the other hand, describes the inflammatory symptoms associated with certain dermatoses. Numerous systemic diseases manifest symptoms through the skin, such as measles and rubella. However, these conditions are not classified as dermatoses. Examples of skin diseases, or dermatoses, include skin cancer, eczema, psoriasis, acne, impetigo, scabies, sunburn, warts, fifth disease (also known as erythema infectiosum or slapped face disease), tinea, herpes, ulcers, and pruritus. Certain skin disorders can result from the absorption of harmful substances through the skin. Failure to use appropriate protective measures, such as gloves, aprons, or overalls, can lead to skin irritation or, in severe cases, poisoning.
